name: Karabair
notes: The Qorabayir - an old Central Asian riding and light-harness horse of the oasis country, kept above all in Uzbekistan and across the border into northern Tajikistan. Uzbek writing calls it a golden fund of the national horse breeding, and it is used for riding, packing, light draught and the mounted games.

The name is usually glossed 'black horse' and the breed is not colour-defined. Bay, chestnut, grey and black are all documented, with no registry colour rule; recent Uzbek literature leans on black and dark bay, which the extension and agouti pools carry rather than an artificial dark shade band.
Grey is a real and visible part of the population at something near a fifth of founders. The rate is a gameplay estimate, not a measured STX17 frequency - no such count exists for the breed.
Every dilution and every white pattern is forced wild. That is an absence of breed-specific evidence rather than a registry prohibition, and it is the conservative reading.
The real main, riding and denser intra-breed types are not strains here. No separate size or colour data was cited for them, and a strain may override gene pools and nothing else.
Tolerant both ways for a continental climate - hot dry summers, cold winters - and neither near-fixed, since this is oasis and foothill stock rather than a high-desert or high-plateau landrace.
All disorders clear. The one breed-health source found states outright that no inherited disease is well documented in the Karabair, while cautioning that absence of evidence is not proof of absence.
The traditional gaits, the mounted games and the regional type differences are none of them modelled.
